Assume Countable Choice. For $a=0,1$ let
$$P_a=D_{a,0}\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^r\operatorname{int}D_{a,i}\subset\mathbb R^2,$$
where every $D_{a,i}$ is the closed bounded region of a smooth embedded circle, the inner disks are pairwise disjoint, and each lies in the interior of the outer disk $D_{a,0}$. The number $r$ is finite and may be zero. Give $P_a$ the plane orientation. After any chosen labeling of the inner boundary components, let $b_i:\partial D_{0,i}\to\partial D_{1,i}$ be smooth diffeomorphisms all preserving their induced boundary orientations, or all reversing them, $0\le i\le r$.

There is a smooth diffeomorphism $B:P_0\to P_1$ extending all $b_i$, preserving orientation in the first case and reversing it in the second. Moreover, for any specified inward smooth collars $c_{a,i}$ of these boundary components into $P_a$, it may satisfy
$$B(c_{0,i}(p,t))=c_{1,i}(b_i(p),t)$$
for every $i$ and all sufficiently small $t\ge0$, with one common smaller collar width. No parametrization of either hole domain or general classification of smooth surfaces is an additional hypothesis or an imported conclusion.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The bounded region of a smooth embedded
circle in the oriented plane, together with its boundary, is a smooth manifold
with boundary diffeomorphic to the closed standard disk. Let $D_0,D_1$ be two
such closed regions. Every orientation-preserving smooth boundary
diffeomorphism $b:\partial D_0\to\partial D_1$ extends to an
orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $B:D_0\to D_1$. More precisely, for
specified smooth inward collars $c_i:\partial D_i\times[0,\epsilon)\to D_i$
with $c_i(p,0)=p$, the extension may be required to satisfy
$B(c_0(p,r))=c_1(b(p),r)$ for every sufficiently small $r\ge0$. In addition, given interior points $p_i\in D_i$ and an orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism $q$ from a neighborhood of $p_0$ onto a neighborhood of $p_1$, the extension can agree with $q$ near $p_0$ while retaining the prescribed boundary collars.

Assume countable choice. Fix integers $m\ge2$, $b\ge1$, $p\ge0$, and positive integers $d_1,\ldots,d_b$ with $\sum_i d_i=m$. There is a compact connected smooth oriented surface $S$ with exactly $b$ boundary components and a positive branched covering
$$\pi:S\longrightarrow\overline{\mathbb D}$$
of degree $m$, unramified near its boundary, such that its boundary components have covering degrees $d_1,\ldots,d_b$. It has exactly
$$N=m+b-2+2p$$
distinct simple interior branch values, each with one ramified preimage of local form $w\mapsto w^2$. Its Euler characteristic is
$$\chi(S)=m-N=2-2p-b.$$
The construction specifies actual charts and a complex structure making the interior map holomorphic. It is a finite slit-gluing construction from a factorization into transpositions; no existence theorem for Riemann surfaces or generic-map selection is assumed.

For degree one a connected positive branched disk cover from a compact surface has no ramification and is a disk mapped diffeomorphically onto the target. Thus positive degree-one covers cannot realize the values $2-2p-b$ above with $b=1,p>0$. This result constructs a surface and covering; it does not identify an arbitrary supplied surface with that surface, realize a given Whitney class, or supply an incidence map into a symmetric product.

derivations.claim: First construct the smooth data on a bounded round planar region. Around its outer circle choose a sufficiently close inscribed polygon, and around each inner circle a sufficiently close circumscribed polygon. All remain disjoint and correctly nested. To arrange finitely many prescribed radial directions, choose a finite angular mesh with successive gaps less than a sufficiently small positive number and containing those directions. Put polygon vertices on one concentric circle of radius $R$ for each boundary component. For an inner circle of radius $r$, require $R\cos(\delta/2)>r$, where $\delta$ is the largest mesh gap; for the outer circle take $R<r$. Thus the polygons and circle collars have positive separation and the polygonal core has the intended holes. Between successive radial directions its boundary collar is one curvilinear quadrilateral. Write $v(s)=(1-s)v_0+sv_1$, $0\le s\le1$, for the intervening polygon side, and choose its smooth argument $\theta(s)$. Since the angular gap is less than $\pi$, $\theta'(s)>0$ and $|v(s)|>0$. [given, construct, algebra]

On an outer collar use $$\Phi(s,t)=\big((1-t)|v(s)|+tr\big)e^{i\theta(s)},\qquad 0\le s,t\le1,$$ and on an inner collar interchange the two radii. These maps are smooth with nonzero Jacobian on a neighborhood of their closed parameter rectangles: the angular derivative is positive and the radial derivative has one fixed nonzero sign. Orient the parameter triangles so that their maps preserve the surface orientation, reversing their vertex order when necessary. The polygon side is parametrized AFFINELY by $v(s)$, and the circle side is its actual smooth circular arc. Split the rectangle by a diagonal. Each resulting triangle has the required smooth nonsingular parametrization. At the radial sides adjacent collar sectors use the same affine interpolation between the same circle and polygon vertices, so their image edges match. Every prescribed boundary point on an initial radial direction is a vertex. [step 1.1, construct, algebra]

Triangulate the remaining polygonal core explicitly, including its holes. Choose a direction with distinct projections of its finitely many vertices. In every slab between successive projections, the boundary pieces are ordered affine graphs; membership alternates at each boundary crossing. The portions of the core in a slab are therefore finitely many convex triangles or quadrilaterals. Subdivide their common walls at all incident vertices and intersections, and fan each convex piece from an interior point. This gives a finite face-to-face affine triangulation of the core. If a core edge was subdivided, subdivide the adjacent collar rectangle at the corresponding $s$ values and fan its smaller rectangles as in step2.1. Thus all images meet face-to-face. Finitely many triangles meet each point and fill its whole disk or half-disk neighborhood; their vertex links are consequently circles or intervals. By [F1] pull this actual finite smooth construction back to each supplied smooth planar piece, with all its prescribed boundary vertices and collars. This is a smooth pullback, not the pullback of a polygonal cellulation by an arbitrary homeomorphism. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

For the finite gluings, first insert in every paired circle the union of both prescribed finite vertex sets, transported by its circle map. Triangulate each piece by step3.1 with those vertices. The two image edges on a paired circle are then the same actual arcs after identification. Their signed product collars make every face parametrization extend smoothly through that seam as a map into the resulting surface chart. Its derivative stays nonsingular there, since the original one-sided collar map extended diffeomorphically across zero. Joining the two boundary half-links makes a circular interior link. The unpaired boundary links stay intervals. This proves clause1. Additional deleted parametrized disks leave finite planar pieces with additional smooth disk holes; apply [F1] again to those pieces. An inserted parametrized annulus is itself a disk-with-one-hole model. Apply the same paired-collar construction to obtain clause2. To use a neighborhood of an original seam, first peel a thin closed signed subcollar around its entire circle from the neighboring pieces and regard that subcollar as one explicit annular piece. The remaining pieces are still planar regions with smooth boundary circles, and the new annulus joins them by its two product rims. A disk around a proper subarc of that seam can now have its whole closure in this annulus interior. Only this explicit finite collar refinement is used; arbitrary intersections of a new disk boundary with the old seams are not presumed finite. [F1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

For clause3 choose disjoint small round disks around the finitely many branch values, wholly inside the base disk. Make them small enough that [F2]'s local branch charts cover every preimage: compactness excludes extra remote preimages approaching a value, and the finite local charts at that fiber give its complete preimage over a smaller disk. Above such a disk are ordinary coordinate disks and, at its one ramified pair, a disk in the coordinate $w$ with projection $q+w^2$. On the complement the cover is unramified. Triangulate that round disk-with-holes by steps1.1–3.1, and lift every closed triangle to its finitely many sheets. A triangle has a simply connected small neighborhood avoiding the branch values; finite continuation of the explicit local sheet inverses supplies one smooth inverse branch on each lifted triangle neighborhood. Equivalently, follow its sheet labels across the finitely many cut banks in [F2]'s construction; no branch point is left there. Thus each lifted face has a smooth nonsingular parametrization in the source coordinate given by that inverse branch, up to its circle boundary. Fill each removed source coordinate disk by steps1.1–3.1 with the same finite boundary vertices. The circle image edges then match those of the lifted complement; their two parametrizations may differ but both are regular increasing parameters on that same smooth arc. Product collars from the actual covering charts give the required smooth seam extension. The degree-one case is simply the disk construction. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct]

Finally convert the finite image incidence data to an abstract simplicial model if necessary. Subdivide each image edge with its own new point, and fan each face from its own interior point, making corresponding subdivisions in the incident Euclidean triangle parameters. A desired point on an image edge has a unique parameter on either of its two regular parametrizations, so the subdivisions match as images. Distinct vertex-edge-face flags now give distinct small triangles; any two intersect in exactly their common flags. Their vertex sets therefore form a finite abstract simplicial complex. Prescribe one common parameter on every image edge and extend each resulting face-boundary homeomorphism over its reference triangle by radial extension; this gives a homeomorphism from the abstract realization to the actual surface. Only this last ABSTRACT realization map is asserted to be topological. The actual smooth triangle parametrizations already constructed in the preceding steps remain available independently on every image face, so no differentiability of that radial extension is needed. All constructions use finite charts, meshes, sheet labels and collars, besides [F1]'s stated Countable Choice. This proves all three clauses with actual smooth face data and no arbitrary-surface smoothing inference. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra] ∎

boundaries.reason: Statement uses finite actual compact surface pieces, not an arbitrary empty-surface theorem.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and step 3.1 include zero inner holes; step 5.1 includes no branch values.
Step 5.1 explicitly includes degree1disk and one-sheet unramified pieces.
Step 4.1 restricts new disk deletion to piece interiors after explicit annular seam refinement; no finite arbitrary seam intersection assumed.
Steps 1.1 and 4.1 retain arbitrary specified finite boundary vertices and paired circle images.
Statement supplies all finite planar/collar or finite-cover data; steps 1.1 through 6.1 give actual local triangles, no arbitrary triangulation or smoothing import.
